conventions: byte strings are 0x-prefixed lowercase hex; `preimage` is the 199-byte control-leaf preimage and `ton_b1`/`ton_b2` its two TON HASHEXT builders (125 + 74 bytes); scenario rows follow committee_transitions_v1.json. `now_ms` is the destination clock: block.timestamp (EVM) or now() (TON) in whole seconds, times 1000, so every `now_ms` is a multiple of 1000; within a scenario `now_ms` never decreases from one step to the next (equal values are calls in the same block or second). Taira-side times (`X.timestamp_ms`, `untilMs`, payload deadlines, fast-pause expiries) are milliseconds and may be sub-second, so a time boundary is probed with the nearest whole-second clock values on both sides. The Taira blocks of `destination_effects` are synthetic destination inputs: every scenario starts from a fresh destination, and the control nonces of a block are chosen for that scenario, so they need not follow Taira's dense per-revision sequence (§4.14.6 step 1). `rejected[].error` is the refusal of the Rust and Python reference when Taira records a control: BadControl is the §3.4 constraint error, and TargetNotExternal, ZeroRevision and ZeroControlNonce are reference labels for the recording rules of §4.14.6 (a route targets an external network, revisions and control nonces start at 1), which no contract reports. `rejected[].destination` is what the destination model answers when such a leaf is certified anyway (null: the leaf does not exist). Row parliament_paused_2 cannot reach a contract through its typed interface (`bool parliamentPaused` on EVM, where the ABI decoder refuses a dirty word, and `Bool` on TON), so no contract harness replays it
